Content is unmistakably Rei Ayanami piloting Evangelion Unit-00: entry 3 (「私は人形じゃない」, "I'm not a doll") is her single most famous line; entries 17/73/100/140 self-report as 零号機 (Unit-00) beginning combat, counterattacking, undamaged, and disabled; entries 0-8 run her classic self-negation monologue (nothing else, only EVA connects her to people, EVA as a mirror, acting on Ikari's/Gendo's wish, her own will, a wish she'll grant); entries 30 and the glossed term Lilith (リリス) place her defending against Lilith directly, and the AT Field vocabulary (110-123) matches the same EVA-pilot register documented for Shinji in section 93. A second voice is bundled in: entries 9, 11, 103, 119, 127 address "レイ" (Rei) by name giving orders/checking on her ("Rei, go", "Get it, Rei", "Good, Rei", "Rei ok?", "Cracked! Rei ok?") -- the same Misato-bundled-into-the-unit's-own-set pattern already documented for section 93 (Shinji/Misato) and section 152 (Mari/Misato); not confirmed by a screenshot but the register (giving combat orders, checking in after damage) matches Misato Katsuragi's established voice exactly. Entries 142-158 are a fourth-wall 'next episode preview' omake bundled onto the end of the set (the same device documented for sections 93/152 and others): 142 has Rei reluctantly agree to read the preview, 143-144 are stock preview narration naming EVA-01 and EVA-00 directly, 145 is the stock 'service, service' sign-off already shipped in section 93 (さあ〜て、この次も、サービスサービスぅ！ -> "Service, service!" at translation/voice_093.json entries 264/282) and 146-158 layer in unscripted-sounding banter about the ぽかぽか(warmth) she feels around Shinji (156) and wanting the player (151-152) and Commander Ikari/Gendo (157, 磇司令) to feel it too. Glossary names kept consistent with this project's already-shipped Evangelion terms (analysis/glossary.json: 磇シンジ -> Shinji Ikari, 綾波レイ -> Rei Ayanami) and with the EVA-0N unit-naming convention already shipped in translation/voice_093.json entry 309 ("EVA-01 pilot, Shinji!") -- carried here as EVA-00/EVA-02 for Unit-00 and Asuka's Unit-02 (entries 85-86, 92, addressed only as "2番目の子"/"2号機のヒト", i.e. "the second child"/"the Unit-02 person", never by Asuka's name in the Japanese -- the name "Asuka" was supplied in English from this project's own already-shipped glossary identification of the Second Child, not invented). Could not verify: entries 9/11/103/119/127's speaker as Misato specifically (vs. some other NERV bridge voice) -- no hard citation, same caveat as section 152's identical pattern. Entry 146 (磇君, budget 2) was left untranslated -- no two-letter rendering of a proper name is a translation rather than an invention, so it ships as the original Japanese per rule 9.

177.why: brief filed unit Strike Freedom Gundam / pilot Kira Yamato on a weapon-match score of 2.3 and explicitly warned not to trust it. Content confirms it is wrong and instead belongs to the Space Demon King's army from the Tetsujin No. 28 crossover (太陽の使者　鉄人２８号): entries 19-21 name 鉄人２８号 (Tetsujin No. 28) and ブラックオックス (Black Ox) as attack targets and entry 20 calls Tetsujin outright '我々の敵だ' (our enemy); entries 15-16 invoke serving 宇宙魔王 (the Space Demon King, '宇宙魔王のために' / '...の命のままに'); entries 33-34 order action against グーラ (Gura) -- 'attempt to capture Milord Gura' then 'erase Gura King Jr.' -- and section 176 (unit Space Demon King, spoken by the King himself in the first person) independently confirms Gura is the King's own son ('聞き分けのない息子には、しつけが必要だ', 'my unruly son needs discipline', entry 20 there), matching the glossary's shared zukan_id 18 for グーラ/グーラ・キング・Ｊｒ． This is the same army as section 108 (General Duncan, who protects Gura and answers to the Space Demon King) and section 176 (the Space Demon King itself), but this section's 109 lines never self-identify a speaker -- no name, no first-person title, only generic self-reference ('本機', 'this unit'). The target-category list also runs far wider than any one story arc (entries 25-32: Mobile Suit, Gundam, Variable Fighter, AT, AS, KMF, android, enemy warship, on top of Tetsujin/Black Ox/Mars-Godmars/Earth Super Robots), which reads as a reusable generic mob/grunt bark table for the King's rank-and-file rather than a named pilot's own lines. Left pilot and unit null and translated with no personal name inserted, per this project's own convention for unresolved generic barks; glossary terms were still used verbatim where they fit budget (Black Ox in full at 21/92/121, Gura at 33/34) and compressed under budget pressure elsewhere (Tetsujin No. 28 -> 'Tetsujin' at 19/91/120; Space Demon King -> 'King' at 15; Godmars/Mars -> 'Mars' at 22/93/122, matching the short form already shipped in section 108). Same conclusion applies to section 178, a verbatim twin of this table (same 109 (Japanese, budget) pairs, just reindexed) per the brief -- it should receive the identical English by propagation rather than a fresh translation pass.

179.review:
Codex draft, Sonnet-reviewed line by line against source/voice/179.json. The identity call itself required no correction (no weapon-table match was on file to override), only the "Ikue Nomura" misnaming in this task's own brief, corrected above to Ikue Sunabara. 18 of 183 lines corrected, grouped by failure type: (1) Dangling orphan line-break -- entries 29 and 59 both shipped literally ending in a bare backslash-n with nothing after it: 29 shipped '21st Century Security
' for 「２１世紀警備保障に負けていられませんぞ！」 (we can't afford to lose to 21st Century Security!), and 59 shipped 'Owe 21st Century Security!
' for 「２１世紀警備保障様には…お世話になっておりますからな！」 (we're much obliged to 21st Century Security!). Both were artifacts, not a deliberate two-line break -- the full glossary company name already consumes nearly the whole budget (the same forced trade-off already shipped in translation/voice_192.json entry 133, 'Ugh!
21st Century Security'), so both were fixed by simply dropping the dangling break: 29 -> '21st Century Security', 59 -> 'Owe 21st Century Security!'. (2) Line's entire content dropped for just the speaker's own name -- entry 33, 「ここは不肖、柿小路梅麻呂にお任せを！」 (leave this to your humble servant, Umemaro Kakikouji!), shipped as bare 'Umemaro Kakikouji!', discarding the actual boast; fixed to "Kakikouji's on it!". Entry 77, 「見ましたか！？この木下藤八郎のウルトラＣを！」 (did you see?! this Ultra C of Touhachirou Kinoshita's!), shipped as 'Touhachirou Kinoshita
C!' -- dropping the "did you see" call-to-attention and mangling the stock idiom "Ultra C" (an amazing, unexpected feat) into a stray floating "C!"; fixed to 'See!
Kinoshita's Ultra C!', restoring both the idiom and the attention-call. (3) Idiom mistranslation -- entry 28, 「おのれ、化け物め！成敗してくれるわ！」 (you wretch, monster! I'll bring you to justice!), shipped as the vague, oddly legalistic 'Beast! Face law!'; fixed to "Beast! I'll punish!", restoring the vow-of-comeuppance bite. Entry 112, 「もう、社長ったら…。ワガママを言っちゃ駄目ですよ」 (honestly, President... you mustn't be so willful/spoiled), shipped as 'Boss... Don't be greedy.', swapping the actual vice (childish willfulness -- not wanting to rest, per entry 113's follow-up) for an unrelated one (avarice); fixed to "Boss, don't be selfish.". Entry 201, 「営業も戦闘もお任せ下さい！」 (please leave both sales and combat to us!), shipped as the unpunctuated fragment 'Sales and war', both dropping the "leave it to us" clause and overscaling 戦闘 (combat) into "war"; fixed to "Sales, combat" (still budget-forced to drop the verb, but corrects the scope). (4) Garbled/ungrammatical line -- entry 132, 「事務の経験が役に立つといいんだけど…」 (I hope my office experience comes in handy...), shipped as the broken 'Office skill, help', reading as two disconnected fragments; fixed to "Office skill helps" (a complete clause, same cell count). (5) Missing terminal punctuation against an exclaiming original -- 160 ('Missile.' for 「ミサイル攻撃です！」, a period where the original shouts; fixed to 'Missiles!', plural to avoid colliding with entry 118's own distinct 'Missile!'), 161 ('Missile, fire' for 「ミサイル、撃ちますぞぉっ！」 -> 'Fire missile!'), 166 ('Barrier! Wow' for 「このバリア、凄いですな！」 -> 'Big barrier!'), 184 ('Beam! Go' for 「ビームを食らえ！」 -> 'Beam!!'), 216 ('Oho! A shake' for 「おほ！少し揺れますな！」 -> 'Oho! Shake!'). Entry 89, 「これなら当たっても問題なしですね、専務」 (even if we're hit like this, no problem, right Exec?), shipped as 'That hit was fine.', dropping the direct address to the Exec every other exchange with him keeps; fixed to "No harm done, Exec!". (6) Unforced overclaim -- entry 219, 「やった！やりましたぞ！」 (we did it!/we managed it!, not necessarily a final victory), shipped as 'Won! I won!', overclaiming a battle victory the Japanese doesn't specify; fixed to "Did it! Yes!". (7) Minor clarity/consistency -- entry 169 ('Shuttle, firm, done!', an ambiguous three-item list) repunctuated to 'Shuttle, firm: done!' to read as two subjects then a verdict. Entry 171 ('Sorry, yet again.' for 「毎度お騒がせして申し訳ございません」 -- the Shuttle's own launch announcement, already established in translation/library/rt_000.json as opening with "Sorry for the disturbance as always") reworded to 'Sorry, as always.' to match the shipped phrase, same cell count. Entry 173 ('Stay past line!' for 「危険ですから白線の外までお下がりください」, ambiguous about which side of the line is safe) fixed to 'Stay behind line!'. Everything else in the 183-line file read as faithful, correctly registered (the office-worker grumbling and 「パーッと」 bravado kept, not flattened), and within budget on the first pass; every name was checked against katakana with no swaps found, and no reversed scolding/threat direction found anywhere. Quality: cleaner than the weaker Codex drafts on file (090/101-era, B-/C+) -- most running jokes (spoon-hiding at 25, the salary/loan pun at 71, the delivery-service slogan at 230, Ikue's hopeful "office experience" line) survived intact -- but the draft left two dangling orphan line-breaks (a genuine truncation bug), dropped two separate speakers' own self-declared names for their boasts, and lost several closing exclamation marks that had a same-cost fix available. Landing around B/B+, on par with the 158/159 Codex-draft-plus-Sonnet-fixes tier. python tools/check_voice.py work/voice/answer/179.json: 0 problems, 183 of 183 answered (post-fix).
179.why: Filed as a Trider G7 shuttle-crew ensemble; confirmed from content, not a weapon-table match (this section's weapon calls are generic warship/mecha barks, nothing self-contained). Every officer of Takeo General Company named in analysis/glossary.json turns up self-naming or being addressed by title. Entry 33 self-declares in full, 「ここは不肖、柿小路梅麻呂にお任せを！」 (Leave this to your humble servant, Umemaro Kakikouji!) -- confirming the section's chief, dominant voice -- and entry 68 has him lament in the third person, 「柿小路梅麻呂、一生の不覚！」 (Umemaro Kakikouji's lasting shame!), matching his established DSCR as the fussy, elderly Executive Vice President/treasurer (source/library/pilots.json i=1, translation/library/pt_000.json), who is addressed throughout by his title alone as 「専務」 (Exec: 16, 24, 26, 34, 76, 89, 98, etc.) and who carries the running gag of fretting over money (repair costs at 62/81/88/175/212, salary at 6/71/110, even electricity at 110). Entry 77 self-declares Touhachirou Kinoshita (「この木下藤八郎のウルトラＣを！」, this Ultra C of Touhachirou Kinoshita's!) and entry 202 again (「この木下、ここは引き下がれませんっ！」, this Kinoshita won't back down here!) -- the Sales Section Chief (営業係長, pilots.json i=3), whose catchphrase 「パーッと」 (go big/all-out) recurs throughout (32, 55, 152, 159, 180) exactly as his DSCR describes (「「パーッと！」が口癖」), and who is separately addressed by his job title 「係長」 (Chief: 181, 193). A third officer answers to 「常務」 (Mgr, Managing Director: 95, 146) and self-refers with the gruff old-man pronoun 「ワシ」 (111, 114, 179, 208), matching pilots.json i=2's Tetsuo Atsui, the technical officer/mechanic who personally maintains the Shuttle (「ワシが整備しとるシャトルだ！」, entry 208, this is the Shuttle I personally maintain!). The fourth voice is addressed directly as 「郁絵君」 (Ikue-kun: 69, 91, 99, 182) and answers in a distinct polite feminine register (92, 100, 132, 142, 187) -- this is the office/accounting clerk of pilots.json i=4, whose glossary full name is Ikue SUNABARA (砂原郁絵), not "Ikue Nomura" as the brief that opened this task named her; no NOMURA (野村) reading occurs anywhere in the source library or glossary, so that name is corrected here. The young company president Watta Takeo (社長/"Boss", entries 4/57/63/64/99/102/112-113/174/205) is addressed throughout but does not clearly self-voice any line in this set -- he pilots Trider G7 itself in his own separate voice file (translation/voice_173.json); this section is the Shuttle crew's own combat/support bark bank, not his. Unit ships as Shuttle (シャトル, analysis/glossary.json), the crew's own support craft, not Trider G7 itself. Register throughout is the small-company comedy the brief called for: running gags about expense-consciousness, the 「パーッと」 catchphrase, Kinoshita's flashy incompetence, Ikue's earnest office-worker hopefulness, and Atsui's gruff mechanic pride, alongside genuine combat peril (105's darkly comic "time to prepare my will", 130's shame at losing the Shuttle, 169-170's despairing farewell). Not confirmed by a screenshot. python tools/check_voice.py work/voice/answer/179.json: 0 problems, 183 of 183 answered.

198.pilot: Akagi Ryunosuke -- JGSDF officer, leader of the 'Nerima Red Dragon' Arm Slave team (Full Metal Panic! crossover roster), an SRW-original comic-relief character whose speech deliberately imitates Char Aznable
198.unit: Arm Slave (Nerima Red Dragon squad, red-shouldered)
198.why: filed as Gundam Mk-II (weapon-match, 2.0), the same beam-rifle/vulcan common-weapon magnet that misfires elsewhere in this project -- wrong, no Mk-II/AEUG content. The section repeatedly self-identifies by the unit's own nickname 'Nerima Red Dragon' (entries 24/78/82/127/148 -- pride and dying-words lines, not a taunt aimed at a third party), while separately naming Dai-Guard (entry 128, 'wasn't Dai-Guard just a fake prop after all?!') and Gundam (entry 54, 'a Gundam over there too?!') as OPPONENTS encountered mid-battle, not the speaker's own machine -- ruling out both Gundam Mk-II and Dai-Guard as the speaker. Web research (srw.wiki.cre.jp) identifies Akagi Ryunosuke as an anime-original JGSDF pilot first added to the SRW franchise in Super Robot Wars W: he leads a squad called exactly 'Nerima Red Dragon' out of Nerima base, piloting red-marked Arm Slaves (this game's roster confirms Full Metal Panic! as a participating series). His defining trait is a theatrical, grandiose speech pattern that deliberately mimics Char Aznable, played for comedy against his actually modest combat record -- which explains this section's boastful 'our performance rivals a Gundam's!' (entry 29), reluctant-admiration lines ('I admit, good hit', entry 117; 'a bad matchup, is it?!', entry 123), and above all entries 52-53, which react to the REAL Red Comet (Char Aznable) appearing as a separate opponent in the same battle -- a parody character meeting the man he impersonates. The anti-Spacenoid/anti-colony lines (18-23) and address of a superior only as 'Captain' (entries 79/83/147) read as generic hardline-military battle taunts consistent with a JGSDF officer's persona, not a settled personal ideology. Section 199 is the brief's stated ~100% twin and should carry this same attribution and the same English lines. Not confirmed by a screenshot.
